newsitem.title: USA: Charter One deal seen good strategic move.
newsitem.headline: Charter One deal seen good strategic move.

text.p: The planned acquisition of RCSB Financial Inc is a good strategic move which will bring Charter One Financial Inc higher-margined assets on the balance sheeet and improved interest rate sensitivity, analysts said.
Charter One, a $14 billion-asset thrift based in Cleveland, is a fast-growing company which acquired FirstFed Michigan Corp in November, 1995 in a deal which more than doubled its size.

Charles John Koch, chairman and chief executive of Charter One, noted in a conference call that the company has participated in 13 mergers since going public almost 10 years ago. There were about seven other mergers prior to Charter One's start as a public company.
In the merger deal announced late Wednesday, Charter One will acquire RCSB, the parent of the Rochester (New York) Community Savings Bank with $4 billion in assets in a $635 million stock deal.
RCSB conducts a retail thrift business in Rochester and Buffalo, N.Y., and is also involved in auto lending and mortgage banking beyond the borders of New York.

Analyst David Dusenbury of Credit Suisse First Boston Thursday raised his rating on Charter One to buy from hold. He said with both immediate and longer term benefits to Charter One he was establishing a 12-month price taget of $55 per share.
Charter One was trading at 46-5/16 late Thursday, down 7/16.

With RCSB shareholders due to get 0.91 shares of Charter One for each RCSB share, the deal was worth $40.00 per share to RCSB holders based on the Thursday afternoon price. RCSB was up 6-1/4 to 40-1/46.
One attraction of RCSB for Charter One, Koch said, was the company's auto finance business which has $1.1 billion of loans on the books.
Leonard Simon chairman and chief executive of RCSB, will join Charter One as a vice chairman.

Simon told the conference call the unit has 113,000 loans at an average duration of two years and an average yield of nine percent. He noted that the unit focuses on the "prime" segment of the market.

Simon said before RCSB decided on the deal with Charter One, it has been thinking of expanding the auto finance unit into Ohio and Michigan. The auto unit has been strong on the east coast of the U.S., primarily in New York, Maryland and Florida.
Dusenbury said Charter One's interest rate posture will be improved because of the addition of shorter duration finance assets and consumer lending capabilities.
Kevin Timmons, analyst at First Albany Co, started coverage of Charter One Thursday with a buy recommendation. He cited the company's record of growth through acquisitions.

Timmons noted that Charter one is seeking to change its balance sheet mix by increasing the proportion of higher margin loans such as consumer loans, commercial real estate loans and commercial and industrial laons. He also noted in the last quarter Charter One's efficiency ratio was 40.5 percent, one of the best in the industry.
Timmons said the RCSB deal brings Charter One, currently doing business in Ohio and Michigan, into New York where there are additional opportunities to grow.
Frank Barkocy, analyst at Josephtal Lyon & Ross, noted that there has been considerable thrift and bank consolidation to date in New York state and more consolidations are expected.

Charter One said in its press release Wedneday night that it expects the transaction to result in cost savings of 25 percent to 30 percent of RCSB's operating expenses, or approximately $21 million to $25 million after tax. The targeted cost savings would come from elimination of duplicative back office operations and other efficiencies to be gained in the merger.
The bank expects a one-time after-tax charge of $50 to $60 million.

Dusenbury, who has a 1997 earnings estimate for Charter One of $3.95 per share, raised his 1998 estimate to $4.55 per share from $4.35. He noted that the company is not using any revenue enhancements in its calculation that the deal will add three to five percent to its earnings by the second quarter of 1998.
Timmons is estimating earnings for Charter One of $3.95 in 1997 and $4.35 in 1998.
The transaction, which needs approval from the Office of Thrift Supervision and shareholders of both companies, is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 1997.
